picks.editorial_note: A sitting UK cabinet minister marked a construction milestone on what will be Britain's most powerful supercomputer, a government-university partnership meant to power drug discovery and climate modeling — a rare case of AI infrastructure investment reaching head-of-government visibility.
picks.title: AI Minister marks milestone on Supercomputer build | News | The University of Edinburgh

picks.editorial_note: NSF added new topics to its $1.5 billion X-Labs initiative, including a dedicated funding call for AI applied to physical systems, signaling sustained federal commitment to AI-adjacent science at national scale.
picks.title: NSF announces 3 additional topics as part of the NSF X-Labs initiative to pursue generational breakthrough science and technology efforts

picks.editorial_note: An international team unified protein sequence and 3D structure into a single language model, a foundational advance for mapping evolutionary relationships that could accelerate structural biology and drug design broadly.
picks.title: Uniting sequence and structure to map the protein universe | Science Tokyo

picks.editorial_note: UCLA researchers demonstrated hardware where the physical material itself computes as a neural network, a step toward energy-efficient 'physical AI' that could reshape how edge and sensor devices process data locally.
picks.title: Toward physical AI: When the hardware becomes the neural network

picks.editorial_note: A $26.5 million ARPA-H award is funding an AI 'co-pilot' to guide non-specialists through medical procedures in rural care settings, a concrete example of AI addressing real healthcare-access gaps, now drawing national press coverage.
picks.title: Reuters covers SRI's work in the ARPA-H-funded PARADIGM program - SRI

picks.editorial_note: A three-year government-backed partnership with the UK's ARIA will expand an AI- and robotics-driven biofoundry at Edinburgh, tying advanced funding agency backing directly to AI-accelerated biological research infrastructure.
picks.title: Funding boost transforms AI-enabled biological research | News | The University of Edinburgh

picks.editorial_note: NSF's new ELEGANT program aims to translate lab-scale semiconductor research into domestic manufacturing platforms for next-generation AI and computing hardware, directly targeting U.S. supply-chain leadership in microelectronics.
picks.title: NSF invests in translating low-dimensional semiconductor technologies to establish U.S. leadership in microelectronics

picks.editorial_note: Integrating the academically-developed, open-source Apertus language model into Proton's privacy-focused Lumo assistant puts a university-built model in front of tens of millions of users, a notable academia-to-industry deployment.
picks.title: Apertus partners with Proton's Lumo AI assistant

picks.editorial_note: A $5 million NSF award backs a three-university effort to build national cyberinfrastructure for privacy-preserving data sharing, addressing a structural bottleneck that limits collaborative AI research across institutions.
picks.title: $5M NSF award to enhance data protections for users nationwide

picks.editorial_note: Part of the DOE's Genesis Mission, this project uses AI to reason over decades of regulatory and scientific evidence for nuclear waste safety cases, an early example of AI entering high-stakes federal safety and policy review processes.
picks.title: AI project reviews nuclear waste safety-case evidence
